metadata.title: fix(metrics): throttle aggregate_all_components with pg advisory lock and configurable interval
metadata.author: msureshkumar88

description:
## Summary

Closes #4467
Part of #2692 (P1 follow-up: throttle background `aggregate_all_components`)

- **Advisory lock**: `aggregate_all_components` now attempts `pg_try_advisory_lock` before running when called from the background loop. If another worker holds the lock, the function returns `[]` immediately — eliminating 74 of 75 redundant full-table scans per 5-minute window on a typical 3-replica × 25-worker deployment
- **Configurable interval**: new `METRICS_AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS` env var decouples run frequency from window size; defaults to `window_minutes × 60` (no behaviour change unless set)
- **Bandit fixes**: resolved B110 `try/except/pass` in `log_aggregator.py` and `audit_trail_service.py`; B105 false-positive in `oauth_manager.py`

## Design notes

- Session-level lock (`pg_try_advisory_lock`) not transaction-level (`pg_try_advisory_xact_lock`) — `_upsert_metric` commits inside the loop, which would auto-release a transaction-level lock and allow concurrent workers back in
- Fail-open: if the lock SQL raises, aggregation proceeds without the lock rather than suppressing it silently
- Lock only attempted when `should_close=True` (background loop path); callers that pass `db=` (backfill, log_search) are unaffected
- Lock ID `6283185307179` chosen to avoid collision with `bootstrap_db.py` (`42424242424242`)

## SQLite (local dev) compatibility

SQLite is fully supported and completely unchanged by this PR:

- `_is_postgresql()` returns `False` for SQLite — both `_try_aggregate_pg_lock` and `_release_aggregate_pg_lock` return immediately without executing any SQL, so `lock_acquired = True` unconditionally
- Single-process `make dev` (uvicorn `--reload`) runs one worker anyway, so there is nothing to coordinate between workers
- `METRICS_AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS` works identically on SQLite — it controls how often the loop sleeps between runs
- No config changes needed for local dev; the SQLite path is fully transparent

## Manual testing

Start the stack with PostgreSQL, multiple workers, a short interval, and DEBUG logging:

```bash
# .env
METRICS_AGGREGATION_ENABLED=true
METRICS_AGGREGATION_AUTO_START=true
METRICS_AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS=15
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
```

```bash
GUNICORN_WORKERS=4 make serve
```

Tail the logs and filter for aggregation activity:

```bash
docker compose logs -f | grep -E "aggregate|advisory|lock|Skipping"
```

**Expected behaviour after this fix** — per interval, exactly one worker runs the aggregation; all others immediately log:

```
Skipping aggregate_all_components: lock held by another worker
```

**Before this fix**, all 4 workers would run the full aggregation simultaneously every 15 seconds with no coordination.

## Changes

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `mcpgateway/services/log_aggregator.py` | `_AGGREGATE_LOCK_ID`; `_try_aggregate_pg_lock`; `_release_aggregate_pg_lock`; lock guard in `aggregate_all_components` |
| `mcpgateway/config.py` | `metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds: Optional[int]` |
| `mcpgateway/main.py` | Use new config field for loop `interval_seconds` |
| `.env.example` | Document `METRICS_AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS` |
| `tests/unit/.../test_log_aggregator.py` | 12 new tests; 98% coverage on new code; all 69 pass |
| `mcpgateway/services/audit_trail_service.py` | B110: log debug instead of bare `pass` |
| `mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py` | B105: `nosec` annotation with explanation |

reviews.author: Lang-Akshay
reviews.body:
Thanks for the PR @msureshkumar88 . 
Please implement following suggested changes 
The advisory lock is a background coordination primitive — not a security gate — so there are no auth-bypass risks. The only concerns are operational reliability issues with the lock implementation pattern.

| # | File                                       | Line     | Severity | CWE     | Description                                                                                                                                                                           |
| - | ------------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | mcpgateway/services/log_aggregator.py      | 46, 58   | Low      | CWE-89  | F-string interpolation of integer constant in raw SQL; not exploitable (constant int, no user input path), but sets a poor copy-paste precedent                                       |
| 2 | mcpgateway/services/log_aggregator.py      | 48–50   | Low      | CWE-703 | Fail-open on advisory lock acquire error: DB errors silently allow un-coordinated parallel execution; operational concern, not a security risk                                        |
| 3 | mcpgateway/services/log_aggregator.py      | 58–60   | Low      | CWE-667 | Session-level lock not guaranteed released on silent `pg_advisory_unlock` failure; pooled connection may retain lock, leading to aggregation starvation in multi-worker deployments |
| 4 | mcpgateway/services/audit_trail_service.py | 171–172 | Info     | CWE-532 | Exception message logged at DEBUG; no production risk at default `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`                                                                                                  |
| 5 | mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py       | 663      | Info     | —      | `# nosec B105` annotation is correctly justified; value is an RFC 8693 token type URI, not a credential                                                                             |
| 6 | .secrets.baseline                          | 4865     | Info     | —      | Line-number drift from new config field insertion;`is_secret: false` marking remains correct                                                                                        |

**Remediation suggestions:**

1. **F-string in raw SQL (Finding 1):** Use `bindparams` to eliminate ambiguity:

   ```python
   result = db.execute(text("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(:lock_id)").bindparams(lock_id=_AGGREGATE_LOCK_ID))
   db.execute(text("SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(:lock_id)").bindparams(lock_id=_AGGREGATE_LOCK_ID))
   ```
2. **Session-level lock starvation (Finding 3):** Document in `_release_aggregate_pg_lock` that if `pg_advisory_unlock` fails silently on a pooled connection, the session-level lock persists until that connection is physically closed.

## Redundant Code

| # | File               | Line(s)    | Type                 | Description                                                                                                               | Suggestion                                                     |
| - | ------------------ | ---------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | mcpgateway/main.py | 1605–1608 | Defensive code smell | `getattr(settings, "metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds", None)` accesses a field always present on the Pydantic model | Use `settings.metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds` directly |

reviews.author: Lang-Akshay
reviews.body:
Nice work on this one. The advisory lock design is solid — session-level (not transaction-level) is the right call given _upsert_metric commits inside the loop, and the fail-open + SQLite no-op paths are handled cleanly. Test coverage is thorough with all lock paths covered.

Two minor non-blocking suggestions:

- main.py L1606: getattr(settings, "metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds", None) could be simplified to settings.metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds since the field is explicitly declared on Settings
- Worth adding a quick Pydantic validation test asserting metrics_aggregation_interval_seconds=0 raises ValidationError to pin the ge=1 constraint

### Neither is a blocker. ✅ Approving.

commits.message:
fix(metrics): throttle aggregate_all_components with pg advisory lock and configurable interval

Prevents 75+ gunicorn workers from running simultaneous full-table scans
on structured_log_entries every 5 minutes (issue #2692).

- Add pg_try_advisory_lock guard in aggregate_all_components so only one
  worker runs aggregation at a time; fail-open on lock errors; no-op on SQLite
- Add METRICS_AGGREGATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS config to decouple run frequency
  from window size, defaulting to window_minutes * 60
- Add 8 unit tests covering all lock paths (skip, acquire, release on
  success/exception, SQLite no-op, fail-open on DB error, db= passthrough)

Closes #2692

Signed-off-by: Suresh Kumar Moharajan <suresh.kumar.m@ibm.com>

chore: add manual verification script for aggregate advisory lock (issue #2692)

Simulates 5 concurrent workers under four scenarios:
- SQLite path: all workers run (lock bypassed)
- PostgreSQL simulation: exactly one worker runs, rest are skipped
- Lock helpers: no SQL executed on SQLite
- Caller-provided db=: lock never attempted

Run with: uv run python scripts/test_advisory_lock.py

commits.message:
fix(test-script): make advisory lock simulation deterministic

The simulated aggregation completes in microseconds with mocks, so the
lock holder could release before other workers attempted to acquire —
allowing a second worker to run and causing spurious failures.

Fix: introduce an all_attempted Event in fake_release_lock that holds
the lock until every worker has called fake_try_lock. Also move all
patches to test level (outside threads) to eliminate concurrent
patch teardown races.

Signed-off-by: Suresh Kumar Moharajan <suresh.kumar.m@ibm.com>
commits.author: Suresh Kumar Moharajan
